Minimal Pairs - Short e and Long a
Minimal Pairs are two words that sound similar, except for one sound.
The sounds short e and long a are quite different.

The short e sound is a relatively relaxed sound. The middle of the tongue rounds slightly upward and the sides of the tongue may lightly touch the top and bottom side teeth. The lips and jaw are loose and relaxed.

The long a is a 2-sound vowel. The tongue is pushed somewhat forward but in a neutral position in the mouth, and then, as the jaw closes slightly, the tongue moves upward until it is near the teeth. The front sides of the tongue touch the inside of the top teeth at the end of the sound.
Here are a list of minimal pairs with short e and long a sounds. As you read them, focus on the difference between the two sounds.

Tag questions are used to ask for clarification and confirmation.
Question tags are short questions at the end of statements.

They are used when we want to:
  • confirm that something is true or not, or
  • to encourage a reply from the person we are speaking to.

1. A positive statement is followed by a negative question tag. Use this when you think the other person will agree by saying 'yes'.
    • You were working at Polygon, weren't you?
    • You are looking for work, aren't you?
    • She has a friend named Jack, doesn't she?
    • He can use information systems, can't he?

  2. A negative statement is followed by a positive question tag. Use this when you think the other person will agree by saying 'no'.
    • You weren't working at Polygon, were you?
    • You aren't looking for work, are you?
    • She doesn't have a friend named Jack, does she?
    • He can't use information systems, can he?
If the main verb is to be or a modal verb, the tag will be the same. For all other main verbs, use the tag do/does or did/didn't. Look at the examples in the chart.

Instructions: Complete the following steps. Fill in the Self-Assessment.

images.text:
Kristi: Whose turn is it?
Adam: It's your turn, isn't it?
Kristi: I've answered the last five questions, haven't I? I'm pretty sure it's your turn, Adam.
Adam: True.
Kristi: What's your biggest weakness?
Adam: I like to put ketchup on my eggs. I don't know. That's a trick question, isn't it?
Kristi: C'mon Adam. You are so draining! Just talk about one weakness that through training or experience you will one day turn into strength. Try it. Here's a pen.

Adam: Um. Maybe wait a bit. Your turn. What's your favorite animal?
Kristi: My favorite animals are ducks.
Adam: Why is that? They talk funny? They are always wet?
Kristi: Ducks are my favorite animals because they are calm on the surface, but underneath the water they are hustling like crazy and getting work done.
Adam: Are you drunk? That is a dreadful answer!
Kristi: What do you mean? That answer explains who I am as a person and gives a good description of who they would want as an editor assistant. It is a great answer, isn't it?
Adam: Yes, it's a good answer. I'm never going to get a job, am I?

Kristi: Adam. We have to keep drilling! You have a lot of experience interviewing, just use that experience to train yourself with for your next interview.
Adam: I'm dreading my next interview. It's such a pain, isn't it?
Kristi: Yes, it's hard, so you need to work hard to get your dream job. Since I was laid-off, I have been to seminars, workshops, read countless books and been to over ten interviews to help me prepare for this, but this time, I think I'm on track. I'm going to dazzle them at BFP. I have everything to gain.
Adam: Good. Then you can get me a job there too.

contents.value: Finding a job nowadays can be very dreadful. A simple e-mail with your résumé doesn't even guarantee that hiring managers will even look at it. One of the best ways is to use LinkedIn. It is a website where you can easily keep track of current job postings and connections. You still have to hustle, but it is less dreadful than other channels. The only thing you need to work on is building a dazzling profile, and employers will contact you. There is no doubt that this will work for you.
